claim: Photosynthetic starch reserves accumulate in Arabidopsis leaves during the day and decrease approximately linearly with time at night to support metabolism and growth.
source_text: Photosynthetic starch reserves that accumulate in Arabidopsis leaves during the day decrease approximately linearly with time at night to support metabolism and growth.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental observations in the manuscript and references to prior work (Gibon et al., 2004; Graf et al., 2010).

claim: The rate of starch decrease at night is adjusted to accommodate variation in the time of onset of darkness and starch content, such that reserves last almost precisely until dawn.
source_text: We find that the rate of decrease is adjusted to accommodate variation in the time of onset of darkness and starch content, such that reserves last almost precisely until dawn.
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript, including Figure 1.

claim: Generation of starch degradation dynamics requires an arithmetic division computation between the starch content and expected time to dawn.
source_text: Generation of these dynamics therefore requires an arithmetic division computation between the starch content and expected time to dawn.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the experimental observations and mathematical modeling that shows division-like behavior is necessary to explain the data.

claim: Two novel chemical kinetic models are capable of implementing analog arithmetic division.
source_text: We introduce two novel chemical kinetic models capable of implementing analog arithmetic division.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on mathematical modeling and theoretical analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Predictions from the arithmetic division models are successfully tested in plants perturbed by a night-time light period or by mutations in starch degradation pathways.
source_text: Predictions from the models are successfully tested in plants perturbed by a night-time light period or by mutations in starch degradation pathways.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data from perturbation experiments shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Arabidopsis mutants with defects in either the accumulation or the degradation of starch have reduced productivity and exhibit symptoms of starvation.
source_text: In the model plant Arabidopsis thaliana this phenomenon is essential for productivity: mutants with defects in either the accumulation or the degradation of starch have reduced productivity and exhibit symptoms of starvation (Usadel et al., 2008; Yazdanbakhsh et al., 2011).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by references to prior published work by Usadel et al., 2008 and Yazdanbakhsh et al., 2011.

claim: The leaf starch content of Arabidopsis increases approximately linearly with time during the day.
source_text: The leaf starch content of Arabidopsis increases approximately linearly with time during the day
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by references to prior work (Gibon et al., 2004; Graf et al., 2010).

claim: More than half of the carbon assimilated via photosynthesis may be stored as semi-crystalline starch granules inside chloroplasts.
source_text: more than half of the carbon assimilated via photosynthesis may be stored as semi-crystalline starch granules inside chloroplasts.
evidence_reasoning: This is established scientific knowledge about plant carbon metabolism.

claim: At night, 95% of starch is utilized by dawn in Arabidopsis.
source_text: At night, starch content decreases approximately linearly with time such that 95% of starch is utilized by dawn (Gibon et al., 2004; Graf et al., 2010).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by prior published work and confirmed by data in the current manuscript.

claim: The pattern of starch utilization is achieved even when darkness comes unexpectedly early.
source_text: This pattern of utilization is extremely robust, and is achieved even when darkness comes unexpectedly early (Graf et al., 2010).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by prior work and confirmed by experimental data in Figure 1A.

claim: The linear pattern of starch utilization at night is likely to be optimal for the efficient utilization of carbohydrate over the light/dark cycle.
source_text: It is also likely to be optimal for the efficient utilization of carbohydrate over the light/dark cycle (Gibon et al., 2004; Smith and Stitt, 2007; Graf and Smith, 2011; Stitt and Zeeman, 2012; Feugier and Satake, 2013).
evidence_reasoning: This is a hypothesis supported by multiple citations and involves reasoning about optimality.

claim: The way in which starch degradation dynamics are generated is very poorly understood despite its importance for plant productivity.
source_text: However, despite the high importance for plant productivity of precise control of starch degradation, the way in which such dynamics are generated is very poorly understood.
evidence_reasoning: This is a statement about the state of scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: Computation of the appropriate starch degradation rate in a normal night requires the circadian clock.
source_text: we have recently shown that computation of the appropriate starch degradation rate in a normal night requires the circadian clock (Graf et al., 2010)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by prior work by the authors (Graf et al., 2010).

claim: The circadian clock indicates how information about the expected time to dawn is obtained.
source_text: which indicates how information about the expected time to dawn is obtained.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the role of the circadian clock in timing biological processes.

claim: Levels of transcripts for starch-degrading enzymes undergo large daily changes, but levels of the enzymes themselves do not.
source_text: Although levels of transcripts for starch-degrading enzymes undergo large daily changes, levels of the enzymes themselves do not (Smith et al., 2004; Lu et al., 2005; Kötting et al., 2005; Yu et al., 2005; and our unpublished data).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by multiple citations and unpublished data from the authors.

claim: An arithmetic division mechanism would likely control flux through starch degradation at a post-translational level.
source_text: Therefore, it is likely that an arithmetic division mechanism would control flux through starch degradation at a post-translational level.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the observation that enzyme levels do not change while activity does.

claim: Post-translational control would permit swifter modulation of the catalytic capacity of abundant proteins than would be possible via transcription/translation.
source_text: Post-translational control would also permit swifter modulation of the catalytic capacity of these abundant proteins than would be possible via transcription/translation.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on established knowledge about the relative speeds of post-translational vs transcriptional regulation.

claim: The starch degradation system constitutes the first concrete realization of arithmetic operations in biology.
source_text: More generally, we also consider analog chemical kinetic schemes that generate addition, subtraction and multiplication operations. To the best of our knowledge the starch degradation system constitutes the first concrete realization of such arithmetic operations in biology.
evidence_reasoning: This is a claim about the novelty of the finding based on the authors' knowledge of the literature.

claim: The rate of starch degradation is appropriately adjusted in response to an unexpectedly early night in plants grown in 12-hr light/12-hr dark cycles.
source_text: Previously, we showed that the rate of starch degradation is appropriately adjusted in response to an unexpectedly early night (imposition of darkness 8 hr after dawn on plants grown in 12-hr light/12-hr dark cycles)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by prior work and confirmed by data in Figure 1A.

claim: Starch degradation is appropriately adjusted in response to an unexpectedly late night (16 hr after dawn).
source_text: Figure 1A shows starch turnover in Arabidopsis grown in 12-hr light/12-hr dark, then subject to unexpected early (8 hr), normal (12 hr), or unexpected late (16 hr) onset of darkness.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Plants grown at different light intensities during the day have different starch contents at the end of the day.
source_text: Figure 1C shows starch turnover in Arabidopsis exposed to different daytime light levels: 90 µmol quanta m−2 s−1 (open squares) or 50 µmol quanta m−2 s−1 (filled squares)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Plants grown at different light intensities adjust their starch degradation rate such that starch is almost completely consumed by dawn.
source_text: Figure 1C shows starch turnover in Arabidopsis exposed to different daytime light levels... Overall, these results demonstrate that the control of starch degradation at night to achieve almost complete consumption at the expected time of dawn can accommodate unexpected variation in... starch content at the start of the night
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the data in Figure 1C showing different starting starch levels but similar end-of-night depletion.

claim: The cca1/lhy circadian clock mutant has an altered starch degradation rate compared to wild-type.
source_text: Figure 1B shows starch turnover in Arabidopsis cca1/lhy mutant grown in 12-hr light/12-hr dark, then subject to unexpected early (9 hr, circles), or normal (12 hr, squares) onset of darkness
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The cca1/lhy mutant retains the capacity to adjust starch degradation in response to an unexpectedly early night.
source_text: Although the rate of degradation is different in a circadian clock mutant with an altered period from that in the wild-type, the capacity to adjust starch degradation in response to an unexpectedly early night is not compromised.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Brachypodium distachyon exhibits similar starch degradation control to Arabidopsis.
source_text: Figure 1D shows starch turnover in Brachypodium grown in 12-hr light/12-hr dark, then subject to unexpected early (8 hr, circles) or normal (12 hr, squares) onset of darkness
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The mechanism underlying starch degradation control is likely present in evolutionarily-distant species of plants.
source_text: It is also likely that the mechanism underlying this control is present in evolutionarily-distant species of plants.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the observation that both Arabidopsis and Brachypodium show similar behavior.

claim: Robust computation of the appropriate starch degradation rate in response to perturbations is consistent with the implementation of arithmetic division.
source_text: Robust computation of the appropriate starch degradation rate in response to perturbations of both the expected time to dawn and starch content is clearly consistent with the implementation of arithmetic division.
evidence_reasoning: This is a logical inference from the experimental observations and mathematical reasoning.

claim: Starch exists as large polymers that are mostly inaccessible within granule matrices.
source_text: The fact that starch exists as large polymers that are mostly inaccessible within granule matrices means that a separate measure is likely required to provide information about the total amount of starch present at any given time.
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about starch structure.

claim: A separate measure is likely required to provide information about the total amount of starch present at any given time.
source_text: The fact that starch exists as large polymers that are mostly inaccessible within granule matrices means that a separate measure is likely required to provide information about the total amount of starch present at any given time.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the physical properties of starch and the need for information about total starch content.

claim: There exists a soluble molecule S whose concentration is proportional to the amount of starch in a granule.
source_text: Hence, we assume the existence of a soluble molecule S whose concentration is proportional to the amount of starch in a granule.
evidence_reasoning: This is a theoretical assumption made for the mathematical models.

claim: There exists a molecule T whose concentration encodes information about the expected time to dawn.
source_text: Therefore, we further assume the existence of a molecule T whose concentration encodes information about the expected time to dawn.
evidence_reasoning: This is a theoretical assumption made for the mathematical models.

claim: In the first model, the T molecule concentration is proportional to the expected time to dawn after a reset time.
source_text: In our first model the T molecule concentration is proportional to the expected time to dawn after a reset-time t (Figure 2B).
evidence_reasoning: This is a feature of the mathematical model described in the manuscript.

claim: In the second model, the T molecule concentration increases with time proportionally to 1/(expected time to dawn).
source_text: In the second model the T molecule concentration increases with time proportionally to 1/(expected time to dawn) between t and t1 (Figure 2C).
evidence_reasoning: This is a feature of the mathematical model described in the manuscript.

claim: Both arithmetic division models fit the experimental data well.
source_text: Output from both models fits our experimental data well.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the model fits shown in Figure 2F-K.

claim: There is variation in the fitted parameters for both models between experimental data sets.
source_text: We note that there is some variation in the fitted parameters for both models (see Tables 3–6), which arises due to variation between experimental data sets even for a single genotype.
evidence_reasoning: This is observed from the parameter values in Tables 3-6.

claim: Variation in fitted parameters could arise from batch to batch variation in expression levels of degradation or clock components.
source_text: Such variation is widely observed for measurements of primary metabolites over the light/dark cycle and could arise from batch to batch variation in expression levels of degradation or clock components.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative explanation for observed variation.

claim: The degradation rate is continuously computed via arithmetic division during the night.
source_text: The first prediction is that the degradation rate is continuously computed via arithmetic division during the night.
evidence_reasoning: This is a prediction from the mathematical models.

claim: A continuously computed degradation rate has advantages in flexibility and potential to recover from unexpected perturbations.
source_text: Such a scheme clearly has advantages in its flexibility and potential to recover from unexpected perturbations.
evidence_reasoning: This is a logical inference about the benefits of continuous computation.

claim: A night-time light period causes starch to accumulate to levels very similar to those present at the end of the day-time light period.
source_text: To test whether this prediction is correct, we interrupted a normal night with a period of light, ending 5 hr before the expected time of dawn. During this night-time light period starch accumulated to levels very similar to those present at the end of the day-time light period.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The night-time light period did not re-entrain the circadian clock.
source_text: We confirmed that the night-time light period did not re-entrain the circadian clock, by monitoring expression of the clock gene LHY (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data on LHY expression shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The starch degradation rate was reset following the night-time light period.
source_text: Comparison of the rate of starch degradation following the night-time light period with the rate before this period, and with the rate that would have been expected over a normal 12-hr night, allowed a robust assessment of whether the degradation rate had been reset.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: The starch degradation rate after the night-time light period was significantly higher than before the light period.
source_text: The rate of starch degradation after the night-time light period was significantly higher than before the light period (Figure 3A–D, insets).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis (p = 1.6 × 10−3).

claim: The starch degradation rate after the night-time light period was significantly higher than the rate expected over a normal 12-hr night.
source_text: The rate of starch degradation after the night-time light period was also significantly higher than the rate that would have been expected over a normal 12-hr night (p = 3.8 × 10−5).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis.

claim: The results from the night-time light period experiment are consistent with continuous re-computation of the degradation rate throughout the night.
source_text: These results are consistent with the prediction that the degradation rate is continuously re-computed throughout the night.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the experimental results showing rate adjustment after the light period.

claim: A factor involved in specifying the relative degradation rates of starch and S molecules must be appropriately set to reproduce the normal pattern of starch degradation.
source_text: The second prediction from the models concerns the effects on starch degradation of perturbations in components of the arithmetic division or degradation apparatus. To reproduce the normal pattern—in which starch is almost completely degraded by the expected time of dawn—our models require that a factor involved in specifying the relative degradation rates of the starch and S molecules must be appropriately set.
evidence_reasoning: This is a prediction from the mathematical models.

claim: Mutants lacking components of the degradation apparatus involved in interactions with S and T molecules may lack the ability to adjust the rate of starch degradation.
source_text: If this idea is correct, we expect that mutants lacking components of the degradation apparatus involved in these interactions may also lack the ability to adjust the rate of starch degradation in response to variation in starch content or time of onset of darkness.
evidence_reasoning: This is a prediction from the models about expected mutant phenotypes.

claim: Six mutants (lsf1, sex4, bam3, bam4, isa3, pwd) each lacking a protein involved in starch degradation show approximately linear decreases in starch content with time during the night.
source_text: To look for a mutant in this category, we imposed an unexpectedly early night on six mutants, each lacking a protein involved in starch degradation (lsf1, sex4, bam3, bam4, isa3, pwd). All six mutants show approximately linear decreases in starch content with time during the night
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The six starch degradation mutants have higher end-of-night starch contents than wild-type plants.
source_text: but they have higher end-of-night starch contents than wild-type plants.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Five of the six mutants (lsf1, sex4, bam3, bam4, isa3) adjusted their starch degradation rates in response to an unexpectedly early night similar to wild-type plants.
source_text: For five of the six mutants, the rates of starch degradation (as determined from linear fits) were lower during an unexpectedly early night (starting 8 hr after dawn) than in a normal night (starting 12 hr after dawn), as is the case in wild-type plants
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data and analysis shown in Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The pwd mutant did not adjust the rate of starch degradation in response to an unexpectedly early night.
source_text: However for the sixth mutant, pwd, the rate of starch degradation was not adjusted in response to an unexpectedly early night (Figure 4E,F)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis (p = 0.01) shown in Figure 4E,F.

claim: PWD may be a node at which information about expected time to dawn and starch content is integrated to set an appropriate rate of starch degradation.
source_text: This finding indicates that PWD—phosphoglucan, water dikinase—may be a node at which information about expected time to dawn and starch content is integrated to set an appropriate rate of starch degradation.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the unique phenotype of the pwd mutant compared to other degradation mutants.

claim: PWD contributes to a cycle of phosphorylation and dephosphorylation of glucosyl residues within starch polymers that is essential for normal starch degradation.
source_text: PWD contributes to a cycle of phosphorylation and dephosphorylation of glucosyl residues within starch polymers that is essential for normal starch degradation.
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about PWD function supported by citations.

claim: Two enzymes—glucan water dikinase (GWD) and PWD—add phosphate groups to starch polymers at the granule surface.
source_text: Two enzymes—glucan water dikinase (GWD) and PWD—add phosphate groups to starch polymers at the granule surface
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about starch phosphorylation.

claim: Two enzymes—SEX4 and LSF2—remove phosphate groups from starch polymers.
source_text: and two further enzymes SEX4 and LSF2—remove them.
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about starch dephosphorylation.

claim: All four phosphorylation/dephosphorylation enzymes are necessary for normal rates of starch degradation.
source_text: All four enzymes are necessary for normal rates of starch degradation
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Loss of GWD almost completely prevents starch degradation at night.
source_text: and loss of GWD almost completely prevents degradation at night (Smith, 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by a citation to Smith, 2012.

claim: Phosphate groups are thought to disrupt the ordered packing of starch molecules at the granule surface, allowing access to starch degrading enzymes.
source_text: The phosphate groups are thought to disrupt the ordered packing of the starch molecules at the granule surface, allowing access to starch degrading enzymes (beta-amylases and isoamylase 3).
evidence_reasoning: This is a mechanistic hypothesis supported by citations.

claim: Removal of phosphate groups is essential for full degradation of starch polymers because the phosphates block the action of beta-amylases.
source_text: Subsequent removal of the phosphate groups is essential for full degradation of the starch polymers because the phosphates block the action of the exo-acting beta-amylases (Baunsgaard et al., 2005; Kötting et al., 2005; Ritte et al., 2006; Hejazi et al., 2009).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The phosphorylation/dephosphorylation cycle is an attractive candidate for integration of factors that modulate flux through starch degradation.
source_text: The cycle as a whole is thus an attractive candidate for integration of factors that modulate flux through starch degradation.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the properties and importance of the phosphorylation cycle.

claim: The phosphorylation/dephosphorylation cycle modifies the granule surface and is a potential candidate for storage of information about starch content.
source_text: Because the phosphorylation/dephosphorylation cycle modifies the granule surface, it is a potential candidate not only for flux modulation but also for the storage of information about starch content.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the location and function of the phosphorylation cycle.

claim: There is a large increase/decrease in the level of phosphate per unit mass of starch over the light/dark cycle.
source_text: Surprisingly, however, we found a large increase/decrease in the level of phosphate per unit mass of starch over the light/dark cycle (Figure 5).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental measurements shown in Figure 5.

claim: The phosphorylation state of the starch granule surface could provide information about starch content through the day.
source_text: We also showed that the phosphorylation state of the starch granule surface could provide information about starch content through the day.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the observation that phosphate levels per unit starch vary over the light/dark cycle.

claim: The analysis may be relevant to a broader class of biological processes where food reserves are just sufficient to permit survival to the expected end of a predictable period without further food intake.
source_text: Our analysis may also be relevant to a broader class of biological processes, where food reserves accumulated in advance of periods of predictable length without further food intake are just sufficient to permit survival to the expected end of the period.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative extension of the findings to other biological systems.

claim: Migrating little stints arriving at their Arctic breeding grounds have sufficient remaining lipid reserves for an average of only 0.6 days.
source_text: For example, migrating little stints (Calidris minuta) arriving at their Arctic summer breeding grounds after a 5000-km journey have sufficient remaining lipid reserves for an average of only 0.6 days (Tulp et al., 2009).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by a citation to Tulp et al., 2009.

claim: During the 4-month fast period of egg-incubating male emperor penguins, lipid reserves are used such that they reach a critical depletion level at approximately the point at which the females are expected to return.
source_text: During the 4-month fast period of egg-incubating male emperor penguins (Aptenodytes forsteri), lipid reserves are used such that they reach a critical depletion level at approximately the point at which the females are expected to return.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by a citation to Groscolas and Robin, 2001.

claim: Unexpected extension of the fast period in emperor penguins leads to catabolism of protein and abandonment of offspring in favor of hunting for food.
source_text: Unexpected extension of the fast period leads to catabolism of protein and abandonment of offspring in favor of hunting for food (Groscolas and Robin, 2001).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by a citation to Groscolas and Robin, 2001.

claim: The rate of reserve utilization in migrating birds and fasting penguins can potentially be computed by arithmetically dividing the reserve levels by the anticipated time of fasting.
source_text: As in Arabidopsis leaves, the rate of reserve utilization in these examples can potentially be computed by arithmetically dividing the reserve levels by the anticipated time of fasting.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative extension of the arithmetic division concept to other organisms.

claim: Cells are able to use proteins to store and process information through networks of interactions.
source_text: It is a longstanding idea that cells are able to use proteins to store and process information through networks of interactions (Bray, 1995).
evidence_reasoning: This is an established concept in cell biology supported by a citation.

claim: Understanding how biochemical networks work and what kind of computations they perform is an ongoing challenge.
source_text: Understanding how such biochemical networks work and what kind of computations they perform is an ongoing challenge (see Deckard and Sauro, 2004; Lim et al., 2013).
evidence_reasoning: This is a statement about the current state of the field supported by citations.

claim: The analysis has underlined the utility of analog chemical kinetics in performing arithmetic computations in biology.
source_text: Our analysis here has underlined the utility of analog chemical kinetics in performing arithmetic computations in biology.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion drawn from the modeling work presented.

claim: This work provides the first concrete example of a biological system where arithmetic computation is of fundamental importance.
source_text: Importantly, we have for the first time provided a concrete example of a biological system where such a computation is of fundamental importance.
evidence_reasoning: This is a claim about the novelty and significance of the findings.

claim: Previous theoretical implementations of arithmetic operations lacked specific biological applications.
source_text: This contrasts to previous work where elegant theoretical implementations of arithmetic operations lacked specific biological applications (Cory and Perkins, 2008; Buisman et al., 2009).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to prior theoretical work.

claim: Analog chemical kinetic approaches may be useful for calculations in synthetic biology applications.
source_text: Analog chemical kinetic approaches may potentially also be useful for calculations in synthetic biology applications (Benenson, 2012)
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative application supported by a citation.

claim: Analog chemical kinetic approaches are likely to prove much simpler to implement than alternative schemes based on digital circuitry.
source_text: where they are likely to prove much simpler to implement than alternative schemes based on much more complex digital circuitry.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative comparison of different computational approaches.

claim: Arabidopsis thaliana and Brachypodium distachyon plants were grown on soil in 12-hr light/12-hr dark with 200 µmol quanta m−2 s−1 illumination at a constant temperature of 20°C for 21 days.
source_text: Arabidopsis thaliana (in the Col0 background, except for cca1/lhy and its wild-type which were in the Ws background) and Brachypodium distachyon (Bd21) plants were grown as in Graf et al. (2010) on soil in 12-hr light/12-hr dark with 200 µmol quanta m−2 s−1 illumination at a constant temperature of 20°C for 21 days.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the experimental methods used.

claim: The granule surface area does not limit the reaction rate as the granule shrinks, consistent with an approximately linear decrease of starch content with time.
source_text: Importantly we assume that the granule surface area does not limit the reaction rate as the granule shrinks, consistent with an approximately linear decrease of starch content with time.
evidence_reasoning: This is an assumption made in the mathematical models to explain the linear degradation pattern.

claim: In both models the degradation reactions occur only in region(s) of granule surface of overall fixed area as each granule shrinks.
source_text: Accordingly, in both models the degradation reactions (for both the starch and the S molecules) occur only in region(s) of granule surface of overall fixed area as each granule shrinks.
evidence_reasoning: This is a feature of the mathematical models.

claim: The assumption of a non-limiting surface area cannot remain true if the granule shrinks to very small volumes at the end of the night.
source_text: Clearly the assumption of a non-limiting surface area cannot remain true if the granule shrinks to very small volumes, as could happen at the end of the night.
evidence_reasoning: This is a logical limitation of the model assumptions.

claim: The models still fit the experimental data well even at times when granules are very small.
source_text: However, our models still fit the experimental data well even at these times (see Figure 2F–K).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the model fits shown in Figure 2F-K.

claim: Arithmetic division can be implemented simply using analog post-translational chemical kinetics.
source_text: Taken together, our modeling results show that arithmetic division (as well as other arithmetic operations) can be implemented simply using analog post-translational chemical kinetics.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion from the mathematical modeling work.

claim: There is variation in the fitted parameters for both models which arises due to variation between experimental data sets even for a single genotype.
source_text: We note that there is some variation in the fitted parameters for both models (see Tables 3–6), which arises due to variation between experimental data sets even for a single genotype.
evidence_reasoning: This is observed from the parameter values in Tables 3-6.

claim: The fit of the two models to the data is equally good.
source_text: As the fit of the two models to the data is equally good, distinguishing between them is currently challenging.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on comparison of model fits shown in Figure 2.

claim: Two critical predictions common to both models can be tested experimentally.
source_text: However, we can test two critical predictions common to both models.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the experimental strategy for testing the models.

claim: The lsf1 and sex4 mutants failed to degrade their entire starch reserve at night after prolonged darkness.
source_text: As Figure 4A shows, during the days following the prolonged dark period the mutant plants failed to degrade their entire starch reserve at night.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The total starch content degraded by the end of each night in lsf1 and sex4 mutants, expressed as a percentage of the starch content at the end of the respective preceding light period, was approximately constant and much lower than that of wild-type plants.
source_text: Instead, the total starch content degraded by the end of each night, expressed as a percentage of the starch content at the end of the respective preceding light period, was approximately constant and much lower than that of wild-type plants (Figure 4B).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The lsf1 and sex4 mutants could adjust their starch degradation rate in response to an unexpected early night.
source_text: Interestingly, the same mutants could also adjust their starch degradation rate in response to an unexpected early night.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data and analysis shown in Figure 4C,D,F.

claim: The values of R for lsf1 and sex4 are compatible with the wild-type value of 1.33.
source_text: As Figure 4F shows, the values of R found for lsf1 and sex4 are compatible with 1.33 (dashed line)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the analysis shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The bam3, bam4 and isa3 mutants showed the same type of rate adjustment as lsf1 and sex4.
source_text: We also found the same type of rate adjustment in bam3, bam4 and isa3 mutants (see Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The bam3, bam4 and isa3 mutants failed to exhaust their starch reserves by the end of the night.
source_text: which also failed to exhaust their starch reserves by the end of the night.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The models make a precise prediction about how the phenotype of incomplete starch degradation can be produced.
source_text: The models make a precise prediction about how such a phenotype can be produced.
evidence_reasoning: This is a prediction from the mathematical models.

claim: For Model 1, two normalization conditions must hold to obtain a linearly decreasing starch content with time and appropriate degradation rate.
source_text: We showed that for Model 1, in order to obtain a linearly decreasing starch content with time, and with the appropriate degradation rate to ensure complete starch depletion at the time of expected dawn, two normalization conditions must hold
evidence_reasoning: This is derived from the mathematical analysis of Model 1.

claim: The first normalization condition ensures that the number of S molecules, and therefore the starch content, decreases linearly with time during the night.
source_text: The first condition ensures that the number of S molecules, and therefore the starch content, decreases linearly with time during the night.
evidence_reasoning: This is derived from the mathematical analysis of Model 1.

claim: The second normalization condition is needed to keep the number of S molecules and the amount of starch strictly proportional.
source_text: The second condition is needed to keep the number of S molecules and the amount of starch strictly proportional, so that both these quantities are fully degraded by the end of the night.
evidence_reasoning: This is derived from the mathematical analysis of Model 1.

claim: If the second normalization condition is not valid and χ < 1, only a fraction of starch approximately equal to χ is degraded by the time of expected dawn.
source_text: We now assume that the second of the two conditions is not valid, and, in particular, that χ < 1. In this case, the starch degradation proceeds at a slower rate, breaking the proportionality between the number of S molecules and the amount of starch.
